Have you tried 1...d5? 👇

ig_caption:
The Scandinavian Defence starts 1.e4 d5: Black challenges White's centre pawn on the very first move. Here it is at three levels.

At 800: after 2.exd5 Qxd5 your queen comes out early, which is fine as long as you know where it goes next. When 3.Nc3 attacks it, the usual homes are a5, d6 and d8.
At 1200: bring the c8 bishop out to f5 before playing ...e6, so it isn't shut in, and play ...c6 to keep White's knight off b5 and d5. Watch the trick: White's bishop on d2 looks at your queen on a5 through the c3 knight.
At 1600: 2...Nf6 waits to take back on d5 with the knight, so the queen can't be chased.

Have you tried 1...d5? 👇

slides.title: At 800: the idea
slides.take: Black hits White's e4 pawn on move one. After the swap, Black's queen takes back on d5.
slides.edge: Bringing the queen out early is fine here, as long as you know where she goes next.

slides.title: At 800: the queen's home
slides.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5
slides.take: 3.Nc3 attacks the queen and brings out a piece at the same time. Black must move her.
slides.edge: The usual homes are a5, d6 and d8. Pick one, learn it well, and stick with it.

slides.title: At 1200: the set-up
slides.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 c6 Bc4 Bf5 Bd2 e6
slides.take: Bring the c8 bishop out to f5 before ...e6, so it isn't shut in. ...c6 keeps White's knight off b5 and d5.
slides.edge: Watch the trick: White's d2 bishop looks at your queen through the c3 knight. If the knight jumps away, your queen is attacked.

slides.title: At 1600: take back later
slides.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Nxd5
slides.take: Black doesn't hurry to take the pawn back. The knight comes out first, then takes on d5.
slides.edge: Now there is no queen for White to chase, so Black loses no time. The usual reply is 3.d4.
